answer: Trust propagates from anchored attestations through walks of at most \(t\) steps on a weighted, reversible graph. For a sybil set \(S\), the probability of escaping it is at most \(t\Phi(S)\), where \(\Phi\) is conductance. A sparse external cut therefore limits reachable trust and, with capped per-node influence, aggregate voting weight. Min-cut transitivity bounds prevent repeated attestations from amplifying that weight; neither a fable, timber-backed identities, nor a reef of colluding accounts alters the bound.
